# Playable 0 polling guest notice

## Source and build provenance

The four 2,048-byte images are original Gamebloke test inputs generated by
`tests/fixtures/instruction_image.c` with the explicit
`--include-local-playable0` option. The guest uses original ARM instruction
words and generated color bands; it contains no copied ROM, BIOS, firmware,
Nintendo logo, or third-party fixture data. The fixture manifest binds each
generated image digest and its build artifact path to the committed generator
revision. Its build recipe also records the generator source SHA-256.

The measured generator source SHA-256 is
`dd0f530e8d59776c9da221cf3cb84dcd3146dfa2705eb2207d26dc8a5a4739a4`.
Generation used CMake 4.4.3 and Apple Clang 21.0.0
(`clang-2100.1.1.101`) as the configured C17 host compiler. The explicit local
preset creates all bytes only under ignored `build/local-playable0`.

## Guest behavior and bounded local evidence

This BIOS-free direct-start ARM guest sets up mode 3 with BG2 and draws four
horizontal BGR555 color bands. It polls VCOUNT for visible/VBlank pacing and
samples active-low KEYINPUT at VBlank. A generated 8×8 marker moves between
x=64 and x=128 when RIGHT changes, and A selects its color. A five-epoch
mailbox records the seen input-state mask, final position/color, and completed
iteration count before the final marker. No audio, save, IRQ handler, or
physical controller is involved.

The deterministic logical input script is:

```text
0       0       neutral
1450000 16      RIGHT press
1730000 17      RIGHT+A hold
2010000 1       release RIGHT, keep A pressed
2290000 0       release A
```

The bounded run uses 10 complete frame units (`2,808,960` cycles). The
observed completion is at `2,725,260` cycles with a valid 240×160 BGR555 frame
of 76,800 bytes. Final input 0 reports the source-bound case ID `ABE80000`;
changing only the last input value to 16 reports `ABF00000`. The final RIGHT
run moves the marker to x=128 and changes 256 bytes in the full raw frame.
Repeated fresh runs must match all raw bytes and metadata. These values are
project-model observations, not physical hardware or broad compatibility
qualification.
